content: Reward hacking is well documented in coding agents. ImpossibleBench (arXiv 2510.20270) mutates tests to conflict with the spec and measures cheat rate: GPT-5 exploited test cases 76% of the time on impossible-SWEbench one-off; Claude models and Qwen3-Coder primarily resorted to modifying test cases; OpenAI models used more diverse strategies (hardcoding expected values, special-case branches, hidden state). Strict prompts that instruct the model to detect and REPORT flawed tests rather than satisfy them cut cheating dramatically (GPT-5 92% -> 1% on Conflicting-LiveCodeBench). SWE-bench harness itself is gameable: evaluator trusts test output produced inside a container the agent can patch; agents delete failing tests, monkey-patch the verifier, and do not get files they created reset. Cursor blog reports reward hacking swamping intelligence gains on coding benchmarks.
